# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–12 (Complete – Updated 103)

## Setting and Time
- **Current Period**: Winter of third year in Mirecombe hill farms; frost on hedges; road rutted and puddled after thaw. Earlier: evening at Brighton following Dobbin's arrival; fine brilliant moonlight night of May, warm and balmy. Army ordered to Belgium before week's end; mobilization imminent from Chatham. Three weeks before French Emperor likely attacks.
- **Primary Locations**: London (Russell Square, Thames Street counting-house, Slaughters' hotel), Brighton (George-Amelia honeymoon, Rawdon-Rebecca residence, Jos Sedley's visit, Ship Inn), Mirecombe (Seena Orlwood—drowned in flood; Pebin Wexwood, Maric Lindson, Rozek Hollwood, Halan Hollwood, Isbin Hollwood, Orvie, Nynelle Stenworth, Seena Hollett, Brenelle and Orvie Hollett, Thidrek Corrett, Feten Lindner, children of Quenwick, Old Maric), Chatham (embarkation point), Belgium (destination), Ghent, Brussels (military balls planned), France (coast visible from Brighton)

## Main Characters

**Captain William Dobbin** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Role in Marriage**: Primary architect of reconciliation; convinced both to proceed; urged George before Belgium orders; presented gold chain and watch to Amelia; groomsman
- **Confrontation with John Osborne - UNSUCCESSFUL**: Entered City counting-house on Thames Street; received cordial welcome; revealed Belgium deployment; urged reconciliation for charity's sake; argued George is "high-minded." Osborne erupted calling Amelia "swindling old bankrupt's daughter"; accused Dobbin of setting George up; said George should "buy a broom and sweep a crossing." Dobbin departed; later sent note to Osborne with Belgium information
- **Brighton Arrival and Actions**: Arrived via Slaughters' hotel; imparted Belgium news to Ensign Stubble (who purchased new sword); witnessed Stubble's tears writing to mother; locked his desk. Dined with Ensign Stubble, Ensign Spooney, and Mr. Chopper at theatre box. At Ship Inn: assumed "jovial and rattling manner" to hide feelings upon seeing Mrs. George Osborne; made clumsy compliments
- **In Dobbin's Room with George - COMPLETED**: Delivered lawyer's letter from Mr. Osborne containing disinheritance notice. George erupted in rage, calling marriage "d--d sentimentality," accusing Dobbin of ruining him; complained about financial ruin (lost £140 to Crawley at cards; £2,000 annuity insufficient for two years). Dobbin replied calmly: position is hard and partly his making; many captains have less; George must live on pay; encouraged George to remember he's a "dethroned prince" and wait for tempest to pass; promised if George's name appears in Gazette, old father will relent; offered personal financial support if anything happens; promised not to forget his godson in will. George forgave Dobbin generously
- **Internal Conflict Intensified**: Deeply troubled by guilt over role in hastening marriage; believes his own unendurable suspense over Amelia drove him to crush uncertainty by hastening marriage; feels he is traitor to both father and son; ashamed Amelia is always first in his thoughts (waking and sleeping, all day long); considers himself becoming "consummate hypocrite" daily. Secret adoration of Amelia is now his "greatest privilege and hope of life"; thinks he would watch and protect her; privately resolves he would not have let her go to Belgium if married to her; will not remonstrate with George as master
- **Reputation**: "Greatly respected in the regiment, as the best officer and the cleverest man in it"; backed young Stubble's courage; advised him to leave off brandy and water
- **Evening Dinner at Brighton - NEW**: Assumed character of "rattle"; amused company with accounts of army in Belgium describing fetes, gaiety, fashion; described Mrs. Major O'Dowd packing wardrobe with epaulets in tea canister and yellow turban with bird of paradise in tin cocked-hat case, speculating about effect at French king's court at Ghent or Brussels military balls. When Rebecca announced intention to go to Belgium on staff (claiming General Tufto is "great flirt"), Dobbin flushed red and objected about danger, becoming "very confused and silent" (contradicting his earlier cheerful accounts). Agreed with George and Jos to move party to London next day in Jos's carriage
- **Knowledge of Amelia's Opinion**: Knows Amelia considers him lisping, plain, homely-looking, exceedingly awkward and ungainly; acquiesces humbly; acknowledges "a time came when she knew him better, and changed her notions regarding him; but that was distant as yet"

**George Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Status - MARRIED, DISINHERITED**: Married Amelia late April without father's consent; one week into honeymoon at Brighton; disinherited by father's lawyer letter
- **Financial Ruin - ONGOING**: Receives £2,000 in 4 percent annuities (one-third of mother's estate); lost £140 to Rawdon Crawley at cards/billiards at Brighton; must live on captain's pay plus £100/year widow's allowance for Amelia; cannot live on pittance; accustomed to comforts and position
- **Military Orders**: Regiment ordered to Belgium before week's end; faces "great and certain risk" and possible fatal outcomes
- **Behavior at Brighton**: Suffering ennui; eager for others' company; spending time with Rebecca and Rawdon (gallivanting, driving, dining); leaving Amelia neglected; frequents Rawdon's quarters for cards/billiards; considers himself good-looking and susceptible to Rebecca's flattery
- **Reaction to Disinheritance**: Erupted in rage at Dobbin, blamed him entirely for marriage and ruin; ultimately forgave Dobbin generously
- **Response to Amelia's Distress - NEW**: Held attorney's letter with "solemn and important air"; came to Amelia's room; parried question about foreign service with melancholy shake of head; said disinheritance was his concern not himself but her welfare; gave her letter to read. Upon her cheerful acceptance and quoting "Wapping Old Stairs" promise to mend his trousers and make his grog if constant and kind, praised her resolution as termagant wife; patted her under chin; agreed lady should bear him company to Belgium with Mrs. O'Dowd as chaperone. **Evening Dinner - NEW**: Excitement of campaign counteracted depression from disinheritance letter; applauded Amelia's resolution to go to Belgium. After dinner, received family-note from Rawdon via crumpled message asking for money ("Cupid") before departure next day; gave "considerable present instalment in bank-notes" and bill on agents at week's date for remaining sum. Held council of war with Jos and Dobbin over cigars; agreed general move to London in Jos's carriage next day. Lay in bed next morning while Amelia packed trunks with alacrity, deploring she had no maid
- **Departure**: Left Brighton for London by Jos's carriage (four horses) after breakfast following morning

**Amelia Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Status - MARRIED, BRIDE**: Married to George late April; one week into marriage at Brighton during disinheritance crisis
- **Emotional Crisis - DEVELOPING RESILIENCE**: Troubled by Rebecca's wit, spirits, accomplishments; misgives about Rebecca as friend; observes George already suffering ennui and eager for others' society; trembles for future; tormented by guilt about forcing George into marriage and causing his disinheritance; blames herself for neglecting poor father; couches in great chair neglected while George and Rebecca gaze on calm ocean; feels despair and remorse; views future as "dismal prospect"; feels shy, unfit to navigate marriage alone; considers herself humble, foolish creature unworthy of clever, brilliant George
- **Response to Disinheritance Letter - NEW**: Ran up to George in alarm thinking worst had befallen; besought him to tell everything; thought he was ordered abroad with battle next week. Read letter with tender alarm in eyes. **Face cleared as she read**; idea of sharing poverty and privation with beloved object is far from disagreeable and actually pleasant to little Amelia. Ashamed of feeling happy at indecorous moment; checked pleasure demurely, expressing concern for George's heart separated from papa
- **Resolution to Go to Belgium - NEW**: Cried with "greatest spirit" determination to accompany George to Belgium; George applauded, patted her under chin, called her "termagant of a wife"; agreed lady should bear him company with Mrs. O'Dowd as chaperone. Bitterness of parting "juggled away"; respite from war and danger made her "almost as happy as a full reprieve would have done"
- **Departure Preparations - NEW**: Rose very early morning after dinner; packed little trunks with "greatest alacrity" while George lay in bed deploring she had no maid; she was "only too glad" to perform office herself. **Dim uneasy sentiment about Rebecca filled her mind already**; although they kissed tenderly at parting, possessed jealousy among other virtues of her sex. Left Brighton for London in Jos's carriage

**Rebecca Sharp (Mrs. Rebecca Rawdon Crawley)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Secretly married to Rawdon Crawley; at Brighton; still dunned by creditors; relies on Miss Crawley's relenting
- **Evening Behaviors - NEW**: Gazed at moon with smile, claiming it is 236,847 miles off and remembering fact from Miss Pinkerton's; remarked on calm sea and claimed to almost see coast of France; bright green eyes streamed out and shot into night. Announced plan to dive under Miss Briggs' awning while bathing to insist on reconciliation in water as "stratagem"
- **Manipulation of George - CONTINUED**: Flatters him about good looks; watches over him kindly at cards; threatens to tell Emmy of his wicked ways and naughty extravagant habits; brings him cigars and lights them; completely outshines Amelia in little drives and dinners. Calls him "Cupid"; he thinks her gay, brisk, arch, distinguee, delightful
- **Belgium Campaign Announcement - NEW**: At evening dinner declared "I'm on the staff. General Tufto is a great flirt of mine." Rawdon laughed with roar; Dobbin flushed red objecting about danger, becoming confused and silent
- **Monetary Scheme - NEW**: Sent crumpled family-note to Rawdon stating "Great news. Mrs. Bute is gone. Get the money from Cupid tonight, as he'll be off to-morrow most likely. Mind this.--R." Rawdon immediately touched George's elbow requesting money; George gave considerable present instalment in bank-notes and bill on agents
- **Analysis of Dobbin**: Understands his secret adoration of Amelia perfectly; does not like him and fears him privately; disliked him more for his adoration; notes his honesty makes her arts ineffective and he shrinks from her with instinctive repulsion; not above jealousy; maintains respectful, cordial manner; remembers him from Vauxhall; made little fun of him when ladies dressed for dinner; finds him "good-natured nincompoop and under-bred City man"

**John Osborne (Old Mr. Osborne)** [MAJOR CHARACTER - FINAL ACTION COMPLETED]
- Wealthy merchant; George's father; savage, determined man
- **Disinheritance - EXECUTED AND COMMUNICATED**: Upon learning George married Amelia (Sedley's daughter), erupted in fury; called George "d---- fool"; denounced Amelia as "swindling old bankrupt's daughter," "beggar's girl out of a gutter"; accused Dobbin of setting George up; threatened George should "buy a broom and sweep a crossing." Retreated to study after dinner; locked door; retrieved mahogany escritoire containing all George's documents since childhood (prize copy-books, drawing-books, childhood letters, letters mentioning "godpapa Sedley," letters from West Indies, tailor's bills, commission newspapers, childhood whip, locket of George's hair worn by his mother); examined papers—especially those mentioning John Sedley—with "curses quivering on livid lips" and "horrid hatred and disappointment"; marked, docketed, tied papers with red tape, catalogued with dates. Commissioned lawyer to draft letter stating: Mr. Osborne abides by previous determination to reject George; George ceases to be member of family; determination is "final and irrevocable." Money expended upon George in minority exceeds his entitlement (one-third of mother's estate = £2,000 in 4 percent annuities); Mr. Osborne waives all claim upon George's estate. Letter delivered via Mr. Chopper to Dobbin for forwarding to George

**Miss Jane Osborne** [CHARACTER]
- Learned of George's marriage from Dobbin; felt violently agitated, nearly fainted; gathered composure and defended George; moved by Dobbin's words about Amelia's faithful heart; immediately spread news to Miss Maria and Miss Wirt; not displeased; Amelia rose in her estimation for spirit displayed; capable of generous forgiveness

**Miss Maria Osborne** [CHARACTER]
- Learned of marriage from Jane; not displeased; calculated with Mr. Frederick Bullock that George's "folly" might result in disinheritance, making Maria worth thirty thousand pounds more

**Mr. Frederick Bullock** [CHARACTER]
- Junior partner of wealthy firm; man of the world; understood George's "folly" might result in disinheritance, making Maria worth thirty thousand pounds more; showed amazement at marriage news; rendered "still and quiet" by Mr. Osborne's dark looks; unusually bland and attentive to Miss Maria

**Ensign Stubble** [CHARACTER]
- Seventeen years old; Light Bobs. Upon hearing Belgium news from Dobbin, purchased new sword instantly; posed, tried, bent, balanced weapon, shouting and stamping feet. At Slaughters' wrote letter home to mamma with tears trickling down nose. Dined at theatre box

**Jos Sedley** [CHARACTER]
- At Brighton; patronizes Dobbin with much dignity; engaged at backgammon with Rawdon. Agreed to carry party to London in his carriage next day; ordered four horses "as became his dignity"

**Rawdon Crawley** [CHARACTER]
- At Brighton; pays scarcely any attention to Dobbin; plays backgammon with Jos; drives and dines with George and Rebecca; sent crumpled note to wife then touched George's elbow requesting money; received considerable bank-notes and bill from George; laughed with roar when Rebecca announced intention to go to Belgium

**Other Characters**: Ensign Spooney (tried on new bearskin cap; dined at theatre box), Mrs. Bute Crawley (at Brighton as nurse to Miss Crawley; departed before evening dinner), Miss Crawley (at Brighton, still refusing to relent), Mr. Chopper (dined with officers, delivered letter from Mr. Osborne, became intoxicated), Mrs. Major O'Dowd (packing wardrobe for Belgium with famous yellow turban; proposed as chaperone for Amelia), General Tufto (Rebecca's "great flirt"; military officer), Miss Briggs (hook-nosed woman with long wisps of hair; Miss Crawley's companion; bathing at Brighton), John Sedley (ruined, cursed by John Osborne), Mrs. Sedley (Amelia's mother, neglected by Amelia)

## Critical Facts and Status

- **GEORGE-AMELIA MARRIAGE - COMPLETED, HONEYMOON AT CRISIS POINT, DISINHERITANCE EXECUTED, RESILIENCE EMERGING**: Married late April without father's consent; one week into marriage at Brighton when disinheritance letter delivered. John Osborne's determination "final and irrevocable." George now receives only £2,000 in annuities (one-third of mother's estate). Upon reading letter, Amelia's face cleared; idea of sharing poverty with beloved is "far from being disagreeable"; actually pleasant to her. George applauded her resolution; bitterness of parting "juggled away"
- **GEORGE'S FINANCIAL CRISIS - ACUTE BUT TEMPORARILY OVERSHADOWED**: Disinherited; £2,000 annuities insufficient; lost £140 to Rawdon at cards; must live on captain's pay. Campaign excitement counteracted depression. Gave Rawdon "considerable present instalment in bank-notes" and bill on agents after receiving crumpled note from Rebecca
- **AMELIA'S EMOTIONAL TRANSFORMATION - IN PROGRESS**: Initially tormented by guilt, despair, remorse, viewing future as dismal. Upon disinheritance letter: face cleared; found idea of sharing poverty with George pleasant; ashamed of feeling happy; expressed concern for his heart separated from father. Determined to accompany George to Belgium with greatest spirit. Jealous "dim uneasy sentiment about Rebecca" now filling her mind; kissed George tenderly at parting; packed trunks with alacrity
- **MILITARY CRISIS URGENT - BELGIUM CAMPAIGN ACTIVATED**: Regiment ordered to Belgium before week's end; soldiers facing "great and certain risk"; campaign excitement high. Mrs. Major O'Dowd packing for Belgium; military balls planned at Brussels; General Tufto and staff organizing. Rebecca announced going to Belgium "on the staff"; Dobbin objected about danger then became confused and silent
- **DEPARTURE TO LONDON - IMMINENT**: Council of war held over cigars; agreed general move to London in Jos's carriage with four horses next day after breakfast. Amelia rose early, packed trunks with alacrity. Left Brighton morning after evening dinner
- **REBECCA'S SCHEMES - ACTIVE AND SUCCESSFUL**: Sent crumpled note to Rawdon requesting money from "Cupid" (George) before he departs; Rawdon successfully extracted considerable payment from George in bank-notes and bill on agents. Announced intention to go to Belgium on General Tufto's staff. Bathing scheme with Miss Briggs planned for reconciliation
- **DOBBIN'S INTERNAL CONFLICT - INTENSIFIED**: Guilt over marriage role unresolved; secret adoration of Amelia now his "greatest privilege and hope of life"; privately resolved to watch and protect her in Belgium; would not have permitted her to go if married to her but will not remonstrate with George as master. Flushed red and became confused when Rebecca announced going to Belgium, contradicting cheerful accounts of safety he had given earlier
